name: NYSAVE (NY Save Animals in Veterinary Emergency)
region_note: HELP PAYING VET BILLS (financial aid - prevents economic euthanasia; apply to several at once, funds go to the vet)
notes:
NYC-SPECIFIC emergency funding for sick/injured pets of low-income NYC residents (all 5 boroughs). At/below NYC poverty level (about $41,100 for 1 person / $58,700 for a family of 4); must first be denied by CareCredit/Scratchpay. Paid to a participating vet; its guidelines set no fixed yearly amount per household. (917) 669-7281 - info@nysave.org - nysave.org.

NYC-SPECIFIC emergency funding for sick/injured pets of low-income NYC residents (all 5 boroughs). At/below NYC poverty level (about $41,100 for 1 person / $58,700 for a family of 4); you must first be denied by CareCredit/Scratchpay. Paid to a participating vet; its guidelines set no fixed yearly amount per household. Apply: (917) 669-7281, info@nysave.org, nysave.org.

Who qualifies, from its own guidelines (read 2026-11-04): you live in the five boroughs; your income is at or below the city poverty level ($41,100 for one person, $58,700 for a family of four); and you have applied for CareCredit, Scratchpay or similar credit and been turned down. For emergencies, not vaccines or routine care. Call 917-669-7281 or email info@nysave.org.

change_log.note: A reviewer asked whether NYSAVE caps grants per household per year. Its program guidelines, read in a browser on 2026-11-04, set eligibility (city poverty level, turned down for CareCredit or Scratchpay) but no yearly amount per household; the only figures on its site are the $2,500-$10,000 yearly grants it gives partner hospitals. The "~$2,000/yr per household" in the research had no source and is removed.
